# LaunchWitness — Final Build Spec

As of 2026-11-14 · GoDaddy Inclusive Innovation Hackathon 2026 (HackerEarth) · Round 2 build Nov 13–20 · submit by Nov 20 · Top 10 announced Nov 30 · onsite finale Pune, Dec 11.

LaunchWitness is a working name.

---

## 1. Pitch

**One line for judges:** "Describe your business. LaunchWitness launches it on GoDaddy and proves everything works before your first customer arrives."

LaunchWitness takes a small seller from a few lines of description to a live business on her own domain: website, business email, and an order form that reaches her inbox. Then it checks every part for real, fixes or undoes anything that fails during launch, and keeps checking lightly afterwards.

**What makes it different.** Most AI builders stop at "your site is ready." LaunchWitness shows the proof: a real test order arriving in her inbox, every check green, and a report with the time each one passed. The safety rules (approve before spending, preview before changing, undo on failure) are what let an AI be trusted to spend money and change settings for a non-technical owner.

**Why it fits GoDaddy.** Small businesses buying a domain, a website and an email is GoDaddy's core business. LaunchWitness uses GoDaddy's Domains, DNS and Email as the engine, not decoration. GoDaddy's own AI tools already help people get online; LaunchWitness adds the missing piece: proof that it all works, before customers find out it doesn't.

---

## 2. Problem and the story

Small sellers either never get their own online presence, or they get one that is quietly broken.

1. **They don't start, because setup is technical.** A GoDaddy survey found 63% of India's small businesses had no website; of those planning one, only 15% owned a domain, and 30% wanted someone to build and manage it for them (DNA India). The survey is several years old: present it as background, not today's figure.
2. **When they do start, it's often half-working.** A March 2026 analysis put DMARC adoption at 44.9% for small businesses vs 75.3% for large enterprises (Cross-Sector DNS & Email Security). A scan of 200 small and mid-size business domains found 36% missing SPF and over two-thirds with no DMARC record (DEV). Result: order emails land in spam, and the owner never knows — she just thinks business is slow.
3. **AI could do the setup, but isn't trusted to.** Buying a domain and changing settings means spending money and risking email. An owner who can't read a DNS record can't check an agent's work.

Open question: find one current (2025–26) India-specific figure on small businesses without websites before the deck.

**Demo persona: Meera.** Meera sells custom cakes from home and takes orders over Instagram DMs. No website, no business email, never touched DNS. She types two lines and pastes her price list. A few minutes later she has meerabakes.in with her real menu and prices, hello@meerabakes.in, and an order form that lands in that inbox. Before she shares the link with a single customer, LaunchWitness places a test order, watches it arrive, and shows her: **"Your business is ready for customers."**

---

## 3. How it works (user flow)

Seven steps from description to proof; Meera does four of them, and only one costs money.

1. **Describe.** A few lines + price list (typed, pasted or photo). No WhatsApp/Instagram API.
   - Claude (one call) returns the business profile (name, products, prices, hours, area, tone) **plus** the site copy (tagline, about, item descriptions) **plus** how customers order: selling point, days of notice, pickup / delivery and delivery charge, whether customers may add a message for an item, the name the seller's UPI app shows, and her food licence (FSSAI) number if given. Plain code then tidies the reply (delivery is never a menu item; extras such as toppers are marked as extras; ordering rules leave the hours line).
   - **Scope guard (v1 = sellers who take orders).** If the business needs bookings rather than orders (salon, tuition, clinic, classes), the Reader says so in one plain sentence and no shop is built.
2. **Review.** She sees the profile as a form and fixes anything wrong. No AI.
3. **Pick a name.** Claude (one small call) suggests ~10 domain names; code checks real availability + price; shows the best 3.
4. **Preview and approve.** Code fills the ONE fixed template, the same for every seller (no per-business code or CSS; category colours come from a fixed palette by position): header with short badges taken only from her data, menu with prices and an Add button per item (a basket that also works without JavaScript; long menus get two columns and a search box), extras listed apart, about, hours, pickup/delivery, "Order on WhatsApp" link (`wa.me`), UPI QR with "Your UPI app should show: <name>", optional FSSAI number in the footer, privacy page. No "Verified" label anywhere. One approval card lists the domain, total cost and every setting to be made. **Nothing is bought or changed until she taps Approve.**
5. **Launch.** Code only: back up DNS, buy the domain (or use a free sandbox subdomain), point it at the server, set up email, put the site live with HTTPS. Each step streams on screen.
6. **Launch check.** Code checks the site opens, HTTPS is valid, email settings are correct, then places a real test order through her form. If anything fails, the Doctor explains it in one sentence, applies a safe fix or undoes the change, and re-checks until green.
7. **Report and watch.** Report headed **"Your business is ready for customers"**: every check, result, time passed. After launch, the same checks re-run lightly on a timer and alert her if something breaks.

**Two launch modes, same code:**
- **Sandbox launch** at `<slug>.<APP_DOMAIN>`: free, real DNS writes on the app's own domain, real checks. Used for development, rehearsals and judges trying it.
- **Full launch** on a purchased domain: run once, for the recorded demo.

---

## 4. Features

Eight core features first; no stretch item starts until all eight run end to end.

| # | Feature | Tier | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Business reader | Core | Description + price list (text or photo) → editable profile + site copy, one Claude call |
| 2 | Name finder | Core | Claude suggests names; code checks real availability and price; shows 3 |
| 3 | Site builder | Core | One fixed template for every seller: badges from data, menu + basket, extras, about, hours, pickup/delivery, order form, WhatsApp link, UPI QR, privacy page |
| 3a | Orders and payment (session 9) | Core | Order date (min notice enforced), pickup/delivery, quantities, totals worked out on the server; per-order UPI pay link + QR (no gateway, no money passes through us); order ID + status page (Received → Confirmed → Paid → Preparing → Ready / Out for delivery → Delivered / Picked up, or Cancelled); seller's order list on her private link; WhatsApp hand-offs via `wa.me` links |
| 3b | Trust and safety (session 9) | Core | Verify the owner's email before any real launch; Claude policy check that can only hold a shop for team review (never launches); "Report this shop" link + admin pause switch |
| 4 | Launch engine | Core | Plan → preview of changes → approval card → execute (GoDaddy Domains, DNS, Email); sandbox + full modes |
| 5 | Launch check | Core | Site resolves, HTTPS valid, email settings present, real test order arrives |
| 6 | Repair during launch | Core | Doctor explains a failed check, applies a playbook fix or undoes from backup, re-checks |
| 7 | Launch report | Core | One page per business: every check, result, timestamp, plus audit log |
| 8 | Light monitoring | Core (light) | Timer re-checks, domain/cert expiry warnings, alert to personal email, "Run checks now" |
| 9 | Full monitoring | Stretch | Daily test order, change detection ("Was this you?"), incident history |
| 10 | /verify page | Stretch | Official Instagram/WhatsApp listed, backed by a DNS TXT record, so buyers spot fakes |
| 11 | MCP server | Stretch | Engine tools over MCP behind the same safety gates |
| 12 | Fleet view | Stretch | Dashboard of all launched businesses |

Out of scope: payment gateways or holding money (UPI pay links only; "Connect Razorpay (after seller KYC)" is future work), appointments/booking, inventory, SMS, WhatsApp Business / Instagram APIs, multiple templates, custom code generation.

---

## 5. Agents

Claude decides and explains; plain code acts and checks. Three steps use Claude; nothing that spends money or changes settings is left to the model alone.

| Agent | Job | Claude or code | Model | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reader | Profile + site copy + ordering details from text or photo; orders vs bookings | Claude, 1 call | Strong (vision + structured output) | Profile JSON + copy (code tidies it) |
| Policy check (session 9) | Is this shop OK to put live? | Claude decides, code holds | Cheap | OK, or "hold for review" + one plain reason; it can never launch or unpause |
| Namer | Suggest names; check availability + price | Claude suggests, code checks | Cheap | 3 available domains with prices |
| Planner | Every action, setting and cost | Code, fixed schema | — | Plan + before/after preview |
| Executor | Run the approved plan step by step, backup first | Code only | — | Step log |
| Checker | Live checks | Code only | — | Pass/fail per check |
| Doctor | Explain a failed check in one sentence; pick a fix | Claude chooses, code applies | Cheap | Fix + re-check result |

A manager loop runs them in order and stops at the approval card. **Doctor playbook (fixed, in code):** undo from backup · re-add MX · re-add SPF/DKIM/DMARC · retry certificate · re-point site address. It cannot write arbitrary settings.

Cost shape: ~3 Claude calls per launch + 1 per failed check.

---

## 6. Launch checks and repair

Repair happens during launch, because that's where setups actually go wrong: settings not spread yet, a certificate failing first time, a mailbox not ready, an email setting missing, a step failing halfway.

| Check | How | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Domain points to the site | DNS lookup against GoDaddy's authoritative nameservers (not a cached resolver) | Re-point, wait, re-check |
| Site opens over HTTPS | Fetch, validate certificate | Retry certificate, re-check |
| Email settings correct | Look up MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC | Re-add the missing record from the plan |
| Test order arrives | Submit the real form; email carries a "Yes, I got it" link | Check mailbox readiness + MX, retry |
| Launch finished cleanly | Step log shows every step done | Resume the failed step, or undo DNS from backup |

**Repair rules:** max 3 attempts per check, then stop and explain in plain words. Repair never spends money. Every attempt goes to the audit log.

**Confirming the test order:** for real sellers the app can't read their inbox (GoDaddy emails mailbox passwords to the account owner only), so the seller taps "Yes, I got it". For the demo mailbox, the checker can also read the inbox over IMAP (password in env).

**Demo failure:** during launch one check fails on purpose (e.g. DMARC missing → orders would land in spam). The Doctor explains, re-adds, re-checks to green. The fault is staged — say so if asked.

---

## 7. Monitoring after launch

Light monitoring is core; full only if time permits. It re-runs launch checks on a timer (GoDaddy's API has no webhooks).

**Light (build now)**

| How often | What |
|---|---|
| Every 15 minutes | Site opens, HTTPS valid |
| Daily | DNS + email settings still match launch; days left on certificate and domain |

- On failure: re-check once a minute later (rule out blips), then Doctor explains + safe playbook fix.
- Anything needing money or her action (renewal, payment): alert only, at 30 / 7 / 1 days before expiry.
- Alerts go to her **personal email**, not the business inbox.
- "Run checks now" button = same checks on demand (this is how the demo shows it).

**Full (if time permits):** daily real test order; change detection ("Was this you? Tap to restore") instead of silent undo; incident history on the report.

**Honest framing:** in the demo everything sits in the app's GoDaddy account, so little can break after launch. Monitoring matters most once it runs on her own account. Pitch it as insurance, not the hero.

---

## 8. Architecture and GoDaddy usage

One GoDaddy Docker VPS (4 vCPU / 8 GB, provided at $0) runs everything; GoDaddy and Claude are called as APIs.

- **Caddy:** HTTPS for the app and every seller site; on-demand TLS with an `ask` endpoint that only approves domains in the DB.
- **FastAPI:** agents, API, monitoring scheduler, and every seller site (served by `Host` header from one template + profile).
- **React (Vite):** seller-facing app, built and served as static files.
- **SQLite:** profiles, plans, DNS backups, check results, audit log.
- **Outside:** Claude API; GoDaddy Domains/DNS/Email (OTE sandbox in dev, `GODADDY_ENV=ote|prod`); SMTP through the app's one mailbox.
- **Secrets** live only in environment variables.
- **Sandbox subdomains** need a wildcard `*.<APP_DOMAIN>` A record → VPS.

| Step | GoDaddy piece | Calls |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Domains API (or `gddy`) | availability, suggestions, price quote |
| Buy | godaddy.com checkout with credit (demo); Domains API purchase only behind guards | purchase after approval |
| Point | DNS API | list records (backup), set A, MX, SPF/DKIM/DMARC |
| Mailbox | Titan email via `gddy` / Email API | create mailbox, poll until ready |
| Host | Docker VPS | A record → VPS; Caddy issues HTTPS |
| Undo | DNS API | write backup back |

**Access limits:** production Availability API needs 50+ domains or ~$20/month spend; DNS API needs ≥1 domain. So: buy the app domain first; check availability via `gddy`, OTE, or free RDAP if production stays blocked.

Say plainly to judges: hosting is the Docker VPS, not GoDaddy's Hosting API.

---

## 9. Safety rules

1. **Approve before spending.** Purchase/mailbox only after Approve on a card showing exact cost.
2. **Preview before changing.** Every DNS change shown as a before/after diff first.
3. **Back up, then undo.** Before any DNS write, save current records as JSON. Failed launch check can write the backup back. Failed mailbox step is retried, not undone.
4. **Scoped actions.** Each launch touches only its own domain. Doctor picks from a fixed playbook; anything else is refused and logged.
5. **Spend guards in code.** `ALLOW_PURCHASE=false` default, hard `MAX_SPEND_USD` cap, purchase only when flag on AND owner approved.

Every step goes to the audit log shown in the report.

---

## 10. Budget

**GoDaddy:** VPS is added to the cart at $0 by organizers. ~$25 in-store credit covers domain + email. Buy on godaddy.com only after organizers confirm credit; use the CLI to explore and manage.

| Item | Paid by | Expected cost | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 vCPU / 8 GB Docker VPS | Organizers ($0 in cart) | $0 | Check out after confirmation |
| App domain | Credit | Cart price; compare with `gddy` | Buy first (unlocks DNS) |
| Titan Pro Light, 1-month term, 1 mailbox | Credit | ~$2–5 | Buy after domain; create hello@ with `gddy` |
| Meera's demo domain | Credit, if room | Cart price | One full launch for the recording |
| Meera's own mailbox | Credit, if room | Another Pro Light month | Likely skip; test orders go to app mailbox (say so) |

If money runs out: skip Meera's domain; full launch on a subdomain; show purchase in dry-run. SMTP tip: if login fails use `smtpout.secureserver.net` with the full address as username.

**Claude: $100, API only, for the product.** None of it for Claude Code.
- ~3 small calls per launch (cents).
- Strong model only for Reader; cheap for Namer + Doctor.
- Dev: saved fixtures, not live calls, for UI work.
- Live link: per-visitor limit, max-token cap per call, daily spend cap.
- Check spend in the Claude console daily.

---

## 11. Submission (HackerEarth, by Nov 20)

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Title | LaunchWitness: from description to a proven, live business |
| Description | Demo video link (YouTube, unlisted) first line, then project brief + link to the build replay page |
| Theme | Open Innovation |
| Demo Link | Live app URL on the app domain, with a free sandbox launch judges can try |
| Repository URL | GitHub repo |
| Source Code | Zip of repo, no secrets |
| Additional File | Project brief PDF |

Build process for judges: one combined claude-replay page of all Claude Code sessions, hosted at `https://<APP_DOMAIN>/build`, plus `docs/BUILD_LOG.md`.

---

## 12. Demo video script (3 minutes, screen + voiceover, no face)

| Time | Scene | On screen | Voiceover |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | Meera | Instagram: price list highlight, orders in DMs | "Meera has customers. She doesn't have a business online." |
| 0:20–0:45 | Describe | Two lines + price list; profile appears; fix one price | "She describes her business the way she'd tell a friend." |
| 0:45–1:05 | Name + approve | 3 domains with prices; approval card; tap Approve | "Nothing is bought until she says yes." |
| 1:05–1:30 | Launch | Step log streams; site live over HTTPS | "Her site, her domain, her email." |
| 1:30–2:15 | Proof + fix | Test order lands in inbox; one check fails (spam risk); Doctor sentence; fix; green | "Before her first customer, LaunchWitness checks everything, and fixes what's wrong." |
| 2:15–2:40 | Report | "Ready for customers" + timer + expiry warning | "And it keeps checking after launch." |
| 2:40–3:00 | Close | Logo + tagline | "Describe your business. LaunchWitness launches it on GoDaddy, and proves it works before your first customer arrives." |

Never buy a second domain on camera. Record a backup run. Rehearse proof + fix until boring.

---

## 13. Judge Q&A

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Doesn't GoDaddy already have AI for this? | GoDaddy's AI helps people get online. LaunchWitness proves it works (a real order in her inbox) and fixes what doesn't, before customers notice. |
| Who owns the domain? | Demo: my account. Real product: her own GoDaddy account, so she owns everything. |
| What can break after launch? | Not much in a setup we control. Real risks: renewal failing, someone changing settings while connecting another tool. Monitoring is insurance. |
| If her email breaks, how do you alert her? | Personal email, not the business inbox. |
| What if she changes a setting on purpose? | Not undone silently; it asks "Was this you?" first (full monitoring). Auto-fix only when a check fails. |
| What if your server goes down? | Checks stop too. Next step: outside uptime pinger. |
| Why trust AI with money and DNS? | It can't act alone: approval, preview, backup/undo, fixed fixes, spend caps in code. |
| Where does Claude matter? | Messy price list/photo → clean profile + copy; brand-fit names; plain-words diagnosis. Code acts. |
| Why VPS not GoDaddy Hosting? | Docker VPS option runs FastAPI + many seller sites with automatic HTTPS from one box. |
| Confirm delivery for real sellers? | "Yes, I got it" link in the test email; no mailbox password [REDACTED] |
| Was the demo failure real? | Staged so it shows reliably; detection and fix are real code. |
| Cost per seller? | A few Claude calls (cents) + domain + mailbox she'd buy anyway. |

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Use it whenever a student wants to plan courses or a semester, set up or update a study/course planner, import new courses from Stud.IP (or HISinOne, LSF, CAMPUSonline, a PDF catalogue), check which courses count toward their degree or admission conditions (Auflagen), add a single course from another catalogue, or change anything in an existing planner — also for German requests like "Studienplaner", "Kurswahl", "Stundenplan planen", "neue Kurse in Stud.IP", "Vorlesungsverzeichnis", even if the word planner is not used. Also answers how to install and set up this skill.
- learning-tutor:learning-tutor: Use when the user wants to learn, study, review, or understand any topic. Acts as a personal tutor guiding the user through programming, math, science, humanities, languages, or any other domain. Triggers on: "teach me X", "explain X", "what is X", "how does X work", "study plan for X", "quiz me on X", "review", "I want to learn X", or equivalent Chinese phrases like "教我", "讲解", "什么是", "帮我理解", "复习", "学习计划", "测验". Also activates when the user asks conceptual questions that go beyond simple factual lookups and require pedagogical structure. DO NOT use this skill for: simple factual Q&A that needs a one-line answer, code debugging, or tasks unrelated to learning/understanding concepts.
- learning-planner:learning-planner: Use when the user talks about learning plans, study schedules, or wants to plan/organize/review their learning progress. Triggers on phrases like "学习计划", "规划学习", "下一阶段", "帮我安排", "学完了", "阶段结束", "总结进度", "plan my study", "learning roadmap", "what should I learn next", "review my progress", "course planning", "skill development plan", "arrange my learning", "学习清单", "学习路线", "学习总结", "阶段规划", organize study, study tracker, progress review. Use this skill whenever a user wants to create, update, or complete a structured learning phase WITH checkbox task tracking and progress summarization.
- learning-framework:learn: Adult learning & knowledge management meta-router — auto-selects from 12 cognitive-science / educational-psychology frameworks (Zettelkasten, Spaced Repetition, Active Recall, Deliberate Practice, Deep Work, etc.). Covers exam prep, certifications, new-field acquisition, knowledge accumulation, expertise growth, and focus retraining. Korean learner context (CSAT / civil service / certifications / 회독 / 오답노트) built-in.
- learning-framework:active-recall: Active Recall (Retrieval Practice) — The testing effect by Roediger·Karpicke. Retrieval (re-test) beats re-study for long-term memory. Pitfalls of highlighting·rereading, the generation effect, desirable difficulty.
- learning-framework:chunking: Chunking — Miller's 7±2 short-term memory constraint, expert chunk perception, and chunk-size calibration in learning design. Meaningless individual items → meaningful chunks = expanded processing capacity. The core representational unit of expertise.
- learning-framework:deep-work: Deep Work — Cal Newport. Distinguishing shallow work from deep work, attention as a muscle, and the four disciplines (monastic/bimodal/rhythmic/journalistic). A framework for designing focused time blocks for knowledge workers.
- learning-framework:deliberate-practice: Deliberate Practice — Anders Ericsson's theory of deliberate practice. Expertise is forged not by time but by *conditions*: specific goals, immediate feedback, just beyond current limits, intense focus. The '10,000-hour rule' is Gladwell-style hyperbole that Ericsson himself refuted.
- learning-framework:evergreen-notes: Evergreen Notes — Andy Matuschak's digital note-taking practice. Concept-oriented, continuously edited, densely linked, atomic. A digital successor to Zettelkasten and more than research notes. Notes are not disposable but *something you come back to and revise*.
- learning-framework:feynman-technique: Feynman Technique — a method of revealing gaps in understanding by explaining to a beginner. 4-step protocol (Choose → Teach → Identify gaps → Simplify). ELI5 approach. The fastest tool to break the illusion of competence.
- learning-framework:interleaving: Interleaving — mixing multiple topics and problem types during study. Compared to blocked repetition, short-term performance ↓ but long-term retention and transfer ↑. Bjork's desirable difficulty. Effectiveness demonstrated in math problem types, sports skills, and language training.
- learning-framework:metalearning: Metalearning — Barbara Oakley *Learning How to Learn* + Scott Young *Ultralearning*. Focused/diffuse modes, illusion of competence, MOC (map of content), learning project design. The upper layer for rapidly acquiring new fields.
- learning-framework:pomodoro-and-focus: Pomodoro Technique (Cirillo 25/5) + focus variants (50/10, 90-minute ultradian). Sophie Leroy's attention residue. Train attention muscle through short focus units + timeboxing tool. The implementation layer of Deep Work.
- learning-framework:second-brain-para: Building a Second Brain — Tiago Forte's personal knowledge management system. PARA (Projects/Areas/Resources/Archives) organization + CODE (Capture/Organize/Distill/Express) workflow. Strong on execution-orientation and project linkage. For when you're drowning in information or stuck on where to put what.

# CLAUDE.md — LaunchWitness

Read this file fully at the start of every session. It is the source of truth for how you work in this repo.

## What we are building

LaunchWitness (working name) — GoDaddy Inclusive Innovation Hackathon 2026, Round 2 (build Nov 13–20, 2026).

> Describe your business. LaunchWitness puts it online on GoDaddy, proves a real order reaches you, fixes what breaks, and keeps checking.

A small seller types a few lines + a price list. LaunchWitness builds her site from one fixed template, buys/points her domain, sets up her email, then **proves** it all works (HTTPS, DNS, email records, a real test order arriving in her inbox), repairs or undoes anything that fails during launch, and keeps lightly checking afterwards.

Full product spec: `docs/SPEC.md`. Milestones and acceptance criteria: `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`.

## Session ritual (every session, no exceptions)

1. **Start:** read `CLAUDE.md`, then `docs/PROGRESS.md` (current milestone, what's done, what's next, open questions). Only read `docs/SPEC.md` / `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` sections relevant to today's task.
2. **Before coding:** state in 3–6 bullets what you will do this session and which acceptance criteria from `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` it targets. Wait for the user's OK if the plan changes anything in `docs/SPEC.md`.
3. **While coding:** small commits, each one working. Run tests before every commit.
4. **End:** update `docs/PROGRESS.md` (move items to Done, set Next, add decisions/open questions) and append one entry to `docs/BUILD_LOG.md` (template inside). Then commit.
5. **Save the transcript:** run `bash scripts/save-transcript.sh <N> <milestone>` (e.g. `2 m2`; set `REDACT_EMAILS=<owner's email>` in the shell, never in a file). It copies this session's transcript to `replay/sessions/<date>-s<N>-<milestone>.jsonl`, redacts the owner's personal email (and any webmail address), replaces each secret-looking value with `[REDACTED]` (strict patterns; code like `password: SecretStr` and base64 screenshot data are not flagged), then re-scans. If anything real-looking remains, it saves nothing and exits 1 — **never commit that transcript**; tell the user which lines matched (it prints line numbers and kinds, never values). Commit the saved file only when the script reports a clean scan. `replay/raw/` stays git-ignored.

## Hard rules

- **No secrets anywhere in the repo.** All keys come from environment variables (see `.env.example`). Never print a secret, never write it to a file other than `.env` (which is git-ignored), never paste it into a commit, test, fixture or log. If you see a secret in a file, stop and tell the user.
- **Never spend money.** Do not run any GoDaddy purchase (domain or email) yourself — not via API, not via `gddy`. Purchases are done by the user on godaddy.com with hackathon credit. In code, purchase paths are guarded by `ALLOW_PURCHASE=false` (default) AND a `MAX_SPEND_USD` cap AND an owner approval record. Never change those defaults.
- **GoDaddy environment:** default `GODADDY_ENV=ote` (sandbox). Production calls only when the user sets `GODADDY_ENV=prod` explicitly. Never write DNS to a domain that is not in the app's own database.
- **Claude API budget is $100 total, for the product only.** During development, do not call the live Claude API for UI work: use saved fixtures in `backend/tests/fixtures/`. Live calls only when a task is specifically about the prompt/agent, and keep `max_tokens` tight. Strong model only for the Reader; cheap model for Namer and Doctor (see env vars).
- **The model never acts alone on money or DNS.** Claude only *decides and explains* (Reader, Namer, Doctor). Plain code *acts and checks* (Planner, Executor, Checker). The Doctor may only pick from the fixed playbook in code.
- **Scope:** build the core features in `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` order. No stretch item until the user says core is done. Out of scope: payments, inventory, WhatsApp/Instagram APIs, multiple templates, generating custom site code.
- **Don't invent product decisions.** If the spec doesn't answer something, pick the simplest option, write it under "Decisions" in `docs/PROGRESS.md`, and mention it in your end-of-session summary.

## Stack

- Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLModel/SQLite, httpx, dnspython, APScheduler, `anthropic` SDK, pytest.
- Frontend: React + Vite + TypeScript, plain CSS (no heavy UI kit).
- Seller sites: server-rendered by FastAPI (Jinja2) from ONE template + the seller's profile, chosen by the `Host` header.
- Infra: one GoDaddy Docker VPS, `docker compose` with `caddy` (HTTPS, on-demand TLS with an `ask` endpoint) + `app` (FastAPI serving API, built frontend and seller sites).
- Email: send via SMTP of the app's one Titan mailbox (`smtpout.secureserver.net`, full address as username, password from env). Read the demo inbox via IMAP (password from env).
- GoDaddy: REST APIs (Domains, DNS, Email) behind one client class, plus `gddy` CLI for manual exploration.

## Repo layout (target)

```
backend/
  app/
    main.py            # FastAPI app, routers, host-based seller site routing
    config.py          # settings from env (pydantic-settings)
    db.py, models.py   # SQLite tables: Business, Plan, DnsBackup, CheckResult, AuditEvent, Approval
    audit.py           # one helper to write AuditEvent rows
    routers/           # health.py (/api/health), internal.py (/internal/tls-ask)
    safety/            # spend_guard.py (ALLOW_PURCHASE + MAX_SPEND_USD + Approval)
    checks/            # dns_resolver.py (public DNS lookups, real + fake)
    agents/            # claude_client.py (fixture|live); reader.py, namer.py, doctor.py (Claude); planner.py, executor.py, checker.py, playbook.py (code)
    integrations.py    # bundle of outside services (fake world or real), FastAPI dependency
    godaddy/           # client.py (ote|prod, scoped DNS writes), availability.py, email.py (mailbox)
    sites/             # templates/seller.html, render.py, hosts.py, routes.py, orders.py
    monitor/           # scheduler.py (light monitoring)
    mail/              # smtp.py, imap.py
  tests/               # pytest; fixtures/ holds saved Claude responses + sample seller inputs
frontend/              # Vite React app
deploy/                # Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile (local), Caddyfile.prod
docs/                  # SPEC.md, BUILD_PLAN.md, PROGRESS.md, BUILD_LOG.md
scripts/               # build-replay.sh and helpers
```

## Commands (keep this section updated as they become real)

- One-time setup: `cp .env.example .env` · `python3.12 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt` · `cd frontend && npm install`
- Backend tests: `cd backend && ../.venv/bin/pytest -q` (or `pytest -q` with `.venv` activated). Tests block all non-local network calls.
- Backend only (dev): `cd backend && ../.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000`
- Frontend dev: `cd frontend && npm run dev` (proxies `/api` to :8000) · build: `npm run build` (FastAPI serves `frontend/dist`)
- Run locally (full stack): `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build` → http://localhost · stop: `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml down`
- Practice mode: `USE_FAKES=true` (default) runs GoDaddy/DNS/mailbox/HTTP against in-memory fakes; set `SERVER_IP`, `USE_FAKES=false` on the VPS once the real integrations exist (see PROGRESS.md "Real integration TODO").
- Live Claude fixtures (owner's laptop; cloud sessions can't hold the key): `bash scripts/capture_all_live.sh` (17 calls, worst case $0.14, cap must be ≤ $1.50, stops at the first failure; details `docs/LIVE_FIXTURES.md`). Single targets: `cd backend && ../.venv/bin/python ../scripts/capture_live_fixtures.py [--dry-run] reader:<seller> | namer:<seller> | doctor:<check>|all` · spend today: `… --report` · strict check: `REQUIRE_LIVE_FIXTURES=1 pytest -q tests/test_s6_agents.py`. Handwritten test image: `.venv/bin/python scripts/make_handwritten_pricelist.py <out.jpg>`
- Team (admin) access in the browser: set `ADMIN_TOKEN` (16+ chars) in `.env`, open `/#/admin`, paste it. The report page then shows the demo fault switch. Owners use their private link (`/#/b/<id>?key=…`, shown once after "describe").
- Monitoring: on by default (`MONITOR_ENABLED=true`, starts with the app); tests never start it.
- Save session transcript: `bash scripts/save-transcript.sh <N> <milestone>` · build replay page: `REDACT_EMAILS=<owner email> bash scripts/build-replay.sh` → `replay/build.html` (served at `/build`; redacts emails, secret-scans the page, deletes it on any hit). One Claude Code session = one file in `replay/sessions/` (the replay keeps one copy per session id: if a chat continues, replace its earlier partial file).
- Prod on the VPS: follow `docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md`. Start/update: `docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build` (Caddyfile.prod, monitoring on, restart always, healthchecks) · M1 check: `bash scripts/check_m1.sh` · DB backup: `bash scripts/backup_db.sh` (restore: `--restore <file>`)
- Demo rehearsal (practice, needs the app running): `python3 scripts/seed_demo.py [--url URL] [--launched]` · reset: `ADMIN_TOKEN` in env, `python3 scripts/seed_demo.py --reset`
- Seller site gallery (6 very different sellers, phone + laptop screenshots): `.venv/bin/python scripts/render_site_gallery.py <tmp_dir> && node scripts/shoot_site_gallery.js <tmp_dir> docs/screenshots/<session>` (warns on sideways scrolling)
- App pages: `/` landing + contact form · `/#/try` describe · `/#/admin` team access · `/build` replay

## Style

- Small, readable modules; type hints; no clever abstractions.
- Every external call (GoDaddy, Claude, SMTP, IMAP, DNS) goes through one wrapper that can be faked in tests.
- Every action that changes state writes an `AuditEvent` (who/what/when/result).
- User-facing text is plain English a non-technical shop owner understands. No "MX", "A record" etc. in the seller UI — technical detail goes in an expandable "details" area.
- Commit messages: imperative, short, prefixed by milestone, e.g. `M2: add DNS backup before writes`.
